2. The story of the prosecution is that on 14.06.2003 at 02:30 PM, at B-1721, Shastri Nagar, Delhi,
within the jurisdiction of PS Sarai Rohilla, accused Rajpal was found in possession of duplicate/spurious gas regulators as well as packing material as detailed in the seizure memo Mark A and B of M/s Indian Oil Corporation and M/s Bharat Gas and further more raw material as well as the machinery used for the purpose of manufacturing of the said duplicate/spurious products were also recovered from the second floor of the aforesaid premises and one pressure dye casting machine, which was used in printing the duplicate hallmarks of Indian Oil Corporation gas regulators were also recovered from the possession of the accused and further the accused also sold one duplicate/spurious gas regulator to the decoy customer Ct. Joginder Singh for Rs. 500/- and thus he also cheated the decoy customer and the accused was also possessing the above duplicate/spurious gas regulator for the purpose of selling the same and thus infringed copyright of M/S Indian Oil Corporation Ltd. and M/S Bharat Gas Ltd.

Secondly, on the aforesaid date, time and place the accused was found selling the aforesaid gas regulator, which were having falsified trademark of M/S Indian Oil Corporation and M/S Bharat Gas and thereby the accused committed an offence punishable u/s 420 IPC r/w 63/65 Copyright Act 1957 and 78/79 TMM Act and within the cognizance of this court.

6. I have heard the arguments addressed by Ld. APP for the State and Ld. Counsel for accused and have carefully perused the documents on record.
7.
Settled proposition of criminal laws are:-
(1) Prosecution is required to prove its case on judicial file beyond all reasonable doubt by leading reliable, cogent and convincing evidence.
(2) Prosecution case needs to stand on its own legs and it cannot derive any benefit whatsoever from the weaknesses, if any, in the defence of the accused.
(3) Burden of proof of the version of the prosecution in a criminal trial through out the trial is on the prosecution and it never shifts to the accused.
(4) Accused is entitled to the benefit of every reasonable doubt in the prosecution story and such doubt entitles the accused to acquittal.

9. The position of the law in this regard has been well established in case titled as "Fateh Singh Mehta Vs. O.P Singhal, AIR 1990 Raj 8, wherein it has been held :-
"Copyright in a work is deemed to be infringed when any person, without a license granted by the owner of the copyright does anything, which is the exclusive right to do conferred by the Act upon the owner of the copyright.

"It is not necessary that the alleged infringement should be an exact or verbatim copy of the original but its resemblances with the original in a large measure is sufficient to indicate that it is a copy."

The case of the prosecution is that on 14.06.2023, the police officials were informed by a secret informer that one Raj Pal has been running a factory at B-1721, Shastri Nagar, Delhi and has been manufacturing spurious Gas Cylinder regulators in the name of Indane and Hindustan Petroleum.

After receiving the said information, Ct. Joginder was deputed as a decoy customer and he was asked to purchase a gas cylinder regulator of Indane Company and one currency note of Rs. 500/-
after noting the number was handed over to him for purchase.
Ct. Joginder purchased the same and handed over the purchased product to IO/Inspector S.K. Gaur.
Thereafter, a raid was conducted on the same date at about 2:25 p.m. at the factory i.e. B-1721, Shastri Nagar, Delhi.
The accused was found at the premises and the said note of Rs.500/- given to the decoy customer was found on a search of the accused.

From the ground floor of the premises, a casted machine/some ready gas regulators and thousands caps of gas cylinders bearing the trademark of "Indane and Hindustan Petroleum" and several dyes having the same FIR No. 178/2003 State v Raj Pal PS: Sarai Rohilla Page No. 17 of 24 trademark were found, which were then seized.

13. In the present case, the prosecution was duty bound to prove the possession of the counterfeit/spurious products with the accused.
Same is sought to be proved by the recovery memo and testimony of the witnesses.

But the manner of conducting inquiry, seizure and search etc. on the spot at the time of arrest of the accused and alleged recovery of counterfeit/spurious products in this case, makes the prosecution version highly doubtful.

The raid in question is stated to have happened at about 02:25 PM on 14.06.2003 and it is evident from the testimony of the prosecution witnesses that the accused was apprehended alongwith the alleged counterfeit/spurious products at his factory, which is a public place but still no public independent person was cited as a witness in this case.
14.
The aforesaid observations have been deduced from the testimony of the prosecution witnesses.

As per version of PW-8/SI Joginder Singh, the IO requested 4-5 public persons/other workers to join the raiding team and investigation, but none agreed and left the spot without disclosing their names and addresses.
He further stated that no written notice was served upon the passersby who refused to join the investigation due to shortage of time.
PW-7/Inspector S.K. Gaur has also stated that he requested 4-5 public persons/other workers to join the raiding team but none agreed and left the spot without disclosing their names and addresses.

The said explanation given by PW-7 cannot FIR No. 178/2003 State v Raj Pal PS: Sarai Rohilla Page No. 18 of 24 MANSI be accepted by the court since, the IO was under obligation to issue MALIK notice in writing to the public persons, who refused to join the police by MANSI MALIK
Date: 2026.01.03 16:33:43 +0530 investigation.

Moreover, the IO has not even placed on record the names of the passerby who were asked to join the investigation and neither have any reasons been mentioned by the IO for refusal by the people who were approached to join the investigation.
In the facts and circumstances of the case, this court finds that police has not made any sincere effort to join independent public witnesses during investigation.

In this regard reliance is being placed on the following judgments:-
In a case law reported as "Anoop V/s State", 1992 (2) C.C. Cases 314 (HC)

, Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has observed as under:
"18.
It is repeatedly laid down by this Court that in such cases it should be shown by the police that sincere efforts have been made to join independent witnesses.

In the present case, it is evident that no such sincere efforts have been made, particularly when we find that shops were open and one or two shop-keepers could have been persuaded to join the raiding party to witness the recovery being made from the appellant.

In case any of the shopkeepers had declined to join the raiding party, the police could have later on taken legal action against such shopkeepers because they could not have escaped the rigours of law while declining to perform their legal duty to assist the police in investigation as a citizen, which is an offence under the IPC".

15. Considering the aforesaid observations made by the Higher Courts, the omissions/ failure on the part of investigating agency to join independent public witnesses create reasonable doubt in the prosecution story.
Making bald averments that 4-5 passersby were asked to join the investigation but none agreed without giving any written notice to them does not inspire the confidence of the Court.
In the circumstances as mentioned above, the recovery of the case property from the accused itself becomes doubtful.

sentences.text: MANSI Infact, no expert from the Indane and Hindustan Petroleum has also MALIK been examined in the matter to identify the genuine from the spurious products and to depose about the differentiating factors between them.

16:34:00 +0530 Further, there is also no evidence to show that the Investigating Officer had sent the seized articles to an expert agency who could have then given a detailed report as to whether the seized articles were genuine or counterfeit.

The normal course of events would be that after the case property was seized in the raid, the same should have been sent to an expert who would have examined the seized articles and the genuine products from the concerned company and then would have given his opinion as to what made them identical or what were the differentiating factors between them.

However, in absence of the testimony of any expert, the Court fails to understand as to how it can be established that the articles/goods alleged to be recovered from the possession of the accused were counterfeit/fake/spurious products.
It is also pertinent to mention here that no document has been placed on record to show that the accused was the tenant/owner of the raided premises.
PW-9/Inspector Manoj Kumar has himself stated in his testimony that he does not remember whether the premises were owned or rented by the accused.
He further stated that no rent agreement/ownership proof was recovered from the accused.
Therefore, it is then not clear as to in which capacity the accused is linked to the raided premises from which the case property has been recovered.

Thus, the prosecution has failed to prove that the accused was the tenant/owner of the raided premises or that the goods alleged to be recovered from the possession of the accused were spurious or that he has infringed the copyright/trademark of Bharat Gas/Indane/Hindustan Petroleum in respect of the seized articles.

sentences.text: Another anomaly which the Court has observed in the instant MALIK case is that it is unclear as to goods of which company have been stated Digitally by MANSI signed MALIK Date: 2026.01.03 to be recovered from the possession of the accused.
The charge which 16:34:06 +0530 has been framed against the accused states that duplicate goods of M/s Indian Oil Corporation Ltd. and M/s Bharat Gas Ltd. were recovered from the accused.

However, in the testimony of PW-7/S.K Gaur,
who was the first IO and who conducted the raid, it has been mentioned that products of Indane and Hindustan Petroleum was recovered from the possession of the accused.
PW-8/SI Jogender Singh who was the decoy customer and was also a part of the raiding party has also deposed that duplicate goods of Indane and Hindustan Petroleum were recovered from the accused.
Therefore, the case of the prosecution is itself unclear as to counterfeit/spurious products of which companies were affected from the accused, raising a doubt on the case of the prosecution.

Further, it is also pertinent to mention here that the existence of copyright/trademark in favour of Bharat Gas/Indian Oil Corporation/Hindustan Petroleum was the basis of the case of the prosecution.

However, the prosecution has not examined any witness from the copyright or trademark office to establish the existence of copyright/trademark in favour of Bharat Gas/Indian Oil Corporation/Hindustan Petroleum.
This hits at the root of the case of the prosecution and demolishes it entirely.

Therefore,
the Court is of the view that the prosecution has failed to prove the essential ingredients of Section 420 IPC r/w 63/65 Copyright Act & U/s 78/79 Trade Mark Act.
18.

Considering the totality of the circumstance, I am of the opinion that the prosecution has miserably failed to substantiate the allegations against accused Rajpal and he is accordingly acquitted for the charges FIR No. 178/2003 State v Raj Pal PS: Sarai Rohilla Page No. 23 of 24 MANSI Section 420 IPC r/w 63/65 Copyright Act & U/s 78/79 Trade Mark MALIK Act as levelled against him.
Ordered accordingly.
